items.title: Devs don't buy Steam disclosure claiming gen AI was a necessity: "I'm literally unemployed and I still make all of my assets by hand"
items.excerpt: After the dark-fantasy idle ARPG Bahast argued on its Steam page that generative AI was a "necessity" to ship on a small budget, other developers pushed back hard, insisting hand-made asset workflows are still viable even while unemployed. A sharp snapshot of the working-designer's stance on 'AI as cost-cutting.'

items.title: Survey finds only 31% of Steam users have a problem with AI in games, with 43% totally fine with it
items.excerpt: A new player survey complicates the loud developer backlash: 43% of Steam users say they're totally fine with generative AI in games and only 31% object, suggesting the audience response to AI-built content is far more split than headlines imply. (This is the verifiable-outlet version of the GameSpot 'players don't care' study, which was Cloudflare-blocked.)

items.title: Sony says AI is "exciting," great for "synthetic assets," and an "important foundational technology supporting our strategy"
items.excerpt: Sony framed AI as a foundational technology for PlayStation, calling it "exciting" for generating "synthetic assets" and central to its content-creation and efficiency strategy across first-party studios — a clear signal of how a platform holder wants AI woven into its production pipeline.

items.title: Dragon Age Creator Calls Gen AI A "Plague" On Game Development
items.excerpt: Dragon Age creator David Gaider called generative AI a "virulent plague" on game development, questioning whether it actually improves the craft ("Does it make the work more efficient? Does it improve the work?") and flagging IP concerns about models trained on creators' work without consent.

items.title: From prompt to reality: how to turn your idea into a physical 3D-printed collectible using Hi3D
items.excerpt: 80 Level ran Hi3D's AI 3D-generation platform through a full pipeline: a single text prompt to concept variations, watertight auto-repaired meshes, and a fully assembled, print-ready miniature — a working text-to-physical-collectible workflow that shows where generative 3D asset tools land for game and character artists.
